topic: 三日坊主 (three-day monk): why you quit and the smaller-floor fix

script.hook: Japanese has one word for people who quit after three days. Here is how to beat it.
points: First, the word. みっかぼうず means a three day monk, someone who gives up after a few days.
Second, the cause. Big plans need big days. One missed hour, and the whole plan feels broken.
Third, the fix. Set a floor, not a goal. Mini mode is fifteen minutes: five words, one grammar point, five minutes of listening. It still counts.
Fourth, miss once, never twice. One missed day is fine. Two in a row is where a habit dies.
script.takeaway: So bad days do not kill a streak. Skipped days do. I built my forty-five day Japanese habit plan on this.
script.cta: Comment forty-five, and I'll send you the link.

social.caption:
Japanese has one word for people who quit after three days: 三日坊主 (mikkabouzu), the three-day monk.

Why it happens: big plans need big days, and one missed hour makes the whole plan feel broken.

The fix: set a floor, not a goal. Mini mode is fifteen minutes: five words, one grammar point, five minutes of listening. It still counts. And miss once, never twice.

I built a 45-day Japanese habit plan on this rule: one page a day, N4 to N3 to an N2 starter.
